findings.finding: October revenue rose 3.2% to $2.04M, supported by higher order volume (+8.4%) and units (+3.9%), while new-customer growth (+4.6%) lagged order growth.
Online drove virtually all net revenue growth: online sales increased $62K (+7.5%) while store sales were essentially flat, up $2K (+0.1%).
findings.explanation: Growth was concentrated in online across all categories; Camping Online grew $25K (+16.5%), and Northeast Camping specifically grew $24K (+20.5%). The October 3–17 cold-weather promotion noted for Northeast Camping is a plausible explanation for that pocket.

findings.finding: West store revenue was the clearest drag, falling $36K (-10.8%); total West revenue declined $18K (-3.2%) despite online growth.
findings.explanation: Client notes report lower foot traffic at two West mall locations, consistent with the store decline.

findings.finding: Returns are a material watchout: returns grew 20.2% to $123K, lifting the return rate from 5.2% to 6.0% (+0.8 pp) as revenue rose only 3.2%.
findings.explanation: The notes flag a new South Footwear Online boot that customers say runs small, but the available return breakdown is only by region, so its contribution to the overall increase is unconfirmed.

findings.finding: Gross margin held up slightly, improving 0.2 pp to 47.7%, with COGS growth (+2.8%) below revenue growth (+3.2%).
Customer acquisition efficiency softened: marketing rose 8.3% and reached 6.5% of revenue (+0.3 pp), while new customers grew more slowly than orders and their share fell 1.1 pp to 31.4%.

executive_summary.text: Revenue rose +3.2% to $2.04M, as order growth outpaced new-customer growth.
Online added +$62K while stores added +$2K, with Northeast leading regional growth at +$42K.
Returns rose +20.2% to $123K, and the return rate increased +0.8 pp to 6.0%.
Marketing rose +8.3% as new-customer share fell -1.1 pp to 31.4%.

slides.title: Revenue grew +3.2% to $2.04M, with order growth outpacing new-customer growth.

bullets.text: New customers grew +4.6%, slower than orders.
Gross margin improved +0.2 pp to 47.7%, while COGS grew +2.8% against revenue growth of +3.2%.

slides.speaker_notes: The findings do not identify a specific cause for the revenue or margin movement.

slides.title: Online added +$62K while stores added only +$2K.

bullets.text: Online revenue grew +7.5%, compared with +0.1% for stores.
Camping Online added +$25K (+16.5%), the strongest cited online category gain.

slides.speaker_notes: The cold-weather promotion noted for Northeast Camping is a plausible explanation for that pocket, but not a confirmed explanation for online growth overall.

slides.title: Northeast led regional growth at +$42K, while West revenue fell -$18K.

bullets.text: South revenue increased +$24K, and Midwest revenue increased +$16K.
West was the only region with a revenue decline.

slides.speaker_notes: Northeast Camping growth is a plausible beneficiary of the noted cold-weather promotion; the cause of other regional changes is not specified.

slides.title: West store revenue fell -$36K despite +$17K growth online.

bullets.text: West store revenue declined -10.8%, while West Online grew +7.3%.
Client notes cite lower foot traffic at West mall locations, consistent with the store decline.

slides.speaker_notes: Lower foot traffic at West mall locations is the likely contributor reported in the client notes.

slides.title: Returns rose +20.2% to $123K, making them a material watchout.

bullets.text: The return rate rose from 5.2% to 6.0%, an increase of +0.8 pp.
A new South Footwear Online boot reportedly runs small, but its contribution to the overall increase is unconfirmed.

slides.speaker_notes: The reported boot fit issue is a possible factor, but the available return breakdown cannot confirm its contribution.

slides.title: Acquisition efficiency softened as marketing rose +8.3% and new-customer share fell -1.1 pp.

bullets.text: Marketing reached 6.5% of revenue, up +0.3 pp.
New customers grew +4.6%, below order growth of +8.4%.
New-customer share of orders declined to 31.4%.

slides.speaker_notes: The findings show weaker acquisition efficiency but do not establish what caused it.
